behavior_items: Defines trait `Sup<T>` with associated type `Assoc: Default`, making each implementation choose a `Default`-constructible associated type per type parameter.
Implements `Sup<T>` for `()` whenever `T: Default`, setting `Assoc = T`; this creates many `Sup<_>` impl instances on the same concrete type.
Defines trait `Dyn<A, B>` as a supertrait combination: `Sup<A, Assoc = A> + Sup<B>`, exercising associated-type equality constraints in trait inheritance.
Implements `Dyn<T, U>` for `()` when both parameters implement `Default`, so `()` satisfies both required `Sup` obligations simultaneously.
Uses a trait object type `dyn Dyn<i32, u32>`, forcing the compiler to reason about object-safe supertraits and inherited associated-type projections.
Projects an associated type from the trait object: `<dyn Dyn<i32, u32> as Sup<u32>>::Assoc`, testing projection through one supertrait of a `dyn` object.
Initializes the projected type with `Default::default()`, so type checking must resolve that projection concretely, expected here to be `u32`.
Exercises compiler normalization and trait-selection logic for multiple supertrait instantiations of the same generic trait on a single trait object.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer builds a trait object `dyn Dyn<i32, u32>` where `Dyn` inherits two `Sup` supertraits with different generic arguments, one constrained by `Assoc = A`. It then projects `<... as Sup<u32>>::Assoc` and initializes it via `Default`. This stresses rustc’s handling of trait-object supertraits, associated-type equality constraints, and normalization when the same generic trait appears multiple times with different parameters.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern points to a compiler ICE in monomorphization/codegen preparation rather than a normal trait error. The reproducer combines: (a) a trait object `dyn Dyn<i32, u32>`, (b) a supertrait list that contains two distinct instantiations of the same generic trait `Sup<_>`, and (c) an associated-type projection through one of those supertraits, `<dyn Dyn<i32, u32> as Sup<u32>>::Assoc`. The query stack ends in `items_of_instance` while collecting mono items for `main`, which suggests type checking accepted or partially accepted the construct, but later stages encountered an invalid or inconsistent internal representation of the trait-object projection/supertrait set. The common pattern is ambiguity or mis-indexing when a `dyn` trait inherits multiple versions of the same generic supertrait, especially with an equality constraint on one inherited associated type (`Sup<A, Assoc = A> + Sup<B>`). A likely compiler defect is in trait-object supertrait elaboration / existential predicate construction / projection normalization, where rustc may incorrectly deduplicate, conflate, or incompletely normalize the two `Sup` supertraits because they share the same trait `DefId` but have different generic arguments. That would later break instance/item collection when codegen asks for the concrete type behind the projected associated type. Another plausible defect is in object-safety or vtable/trait-upcasting metadata construction for dyn predicates containing repeated generic supertraits, causing an impossible `Instance` or malformed associated-item lookup to survive until mono-item collection.
possible_causes: Bug in trait-object supertrait elaboration for `dyn Dyn<A, B>`: rustc may incorrectly merge or deduplicate repeated generic supertraits `Sup<A>` and `Sup<B>` based only on the trait identity, ignoring differing generic arguments.

Bug in associated-type projection normalization for trait objects: `<dyn Dyn<i32, u32> as Sup<u32>>::Assoc` may resolve through the wrong supertrait instance or an incompletely normalized existential predicate set.

Defect in handling associated-type equality constraints on one of multiple inherited instantiations of the same trait (`Sup<A, Assoc = A> + Sup<B>`), leading to an inconsistent internal obligation environment.

Bug in object-safe dyn metadata/vtable construction or supertrait candidate enumeration when the same generic trait appears multiple times with different substitutions, later surfacing during `items_of_instance` collection.
Incorrect canonicalization or caching of projection/trait-selection results for repeated supertraits on dyn objects, causing a stale or mismatched projection result to reach monomorphization.

Missing validation/rejection path in the compiler for unsupported or ambiguous dyn supertrait layouts involving multiple instantiations of the same generic trait, resulting in an ICE instead of a diagnostic.
evidence: The reproducer specifically uses a trait object with multiple supertraits that are different instantiations of the same generic trait: `Dyn<A, B>: Sup<A, Assoc = A> + Sup<B>`.

The projected type is taken through one selected supertrait of the trait object: `<dyn Dyn<i32, u32> as Sup<u32>>::Assoc`, directly stressing supertrait resolution and projection normalization on `dyn` types.

The `Sup<T>` impl for `()` sets `Assoc = T`, so the compiler should concretely infer the projection as `u32`; any ambiguity indicates a compiler-side failure in distinguishing `Sup<i32>` from `Sup<u32>`.

The query stack shows panic in `items_of_instance` / `collect_and_partition_mono_items`, meaning the compiler progressed beyond parsing and likely beyond basic type checking, then failed when later stages consumed an invalid internal type/instance.
The test behavior summary explicitly stresses normalization and trait-selection logic for multiple supertrait instantiations of the same generic trait on a single trait object.

No reproducer-side undefined behavior or unsafe code is involved; the crash is triggered purely by trait-system features (trait objects, supertraits, associated types, equality constraints), which strongly implicates compiler production code in trait solving / normalization / dyn handling.

selected_files.reason: Most suspicious because the reproducer centers on projecting an associated type from a dyn object through one of multiple supertrait instantiations of the same generic trait (`<dyn Dyn<i32, u32> as Sup<u32>>::Assoc`). This file contains the projection candidate logic for associated types, including object-bound candidates, ambiguity handling, and normalization. A bug here could easily conflate `Sup<i32>` and `Sup<u32>` or mishandle the equality-constrained supertrait set, producing an invalid projection result that survives until mono-item collection.

The dyn object type itself is unusual: `dyn Dyn<i32, u32>` where `Dyn` inherits two different instantiations of the same generic supertrait. This file lowers trait-object bounds and enforces dyn-compatibility/object-safety rules. If rustc should reject, normalize differently, or record existential predicates more carefully for repeated generic supertraits, an error here could admit a malformed internal dyn predicate set that later ICEs.

Repeated generic supertraits on a trait object can confuse supertrait enumeration and vtable-segment construction. Even though the panic appears during mono-item collection, malformed trait-object metadata or supertrait traversal can surface later when codegen asks for instances/items associated with the dyn type. This file specifically walks supertrait graphs and lays out trait-owned segments, so deduplication or ordering bugs involving `Sup<A>` and `Sup<B>` are plausible.

This is the middle-layer representation of trait-object vtable entries and supertrait vptr structure. If repeated generic supertraits are represented incorrectly—e.g. merged by trait DefId rather than full substituted trait-ref—the resulting vtable metadata could become inconsistent and later trigger an ICE during instance/item collection.

The query stack ends at `items_of_instance` during mono-item collection, making the collector a strong surface site for the crash. While likely not the root semantic bug, this module consumes resolved instances and MIR mentions; if it assumes a valid instance/projection for dyn-supertrait-associated items and encounters an impossible one, the ICE can manifest here. It is therefore highly suspicious as either the crash site or missing-validation site.

If projection through the dyn supertrait produces a callable/item lookup that must be turned into a concrete `Instance`, this file is a candidate because it resolves associated items and synthesizes shims for codegen. A malformed trait ref arising from `Sup<u32>` on `dyn Dyn<i32, u32>` could cause incorrect instance resolution or an impossible `InstanceKind` that later breaks `items_of_instance`.

The panic query is explicitly about `items_of_instance`, and this file defines `ty::Instance` plus logic/helpers around synthesized shims and callable representations. If the compiler constructs an invalid instance for a trait-object-supertrait projection case, the bug could live in these instance invariants or helper paths rather than in backend code.

The reproducer depends on elaborating supertraits from `Dyn<A, B>: Sup<A, Assoc = A> + Sup<B>`. This file performs predicate elaboration over supertraits and implied predicates. A bug in elaboration or deduplication could collapse the two `Sup<_>` predicates together, lose substitutions, or mishandle the associated-type equality clause, poisoning later projection and dyn-object reasoning.

This file contains predicate deduplication helpers that anonymize and store predicates in sets. Since the reproducer is sensitive to having two supertraits with the same trait DefId but different generic arguments, any over-aggressive normalization/anonymization or set-keying mistake could wrongly deduplicate `Sup<i32>` and `Sup<u32>` in trait-object or elaboration contexts.

Bounds lowering is relevant because the supertrait list includes both a plain `Sup<B>` bound and an associated-type equality bound `Sup<A, Assoc = A>`. If lowering misorders, merges, or incompletely records these bounds for trait objects/supertraits, it could seed the downstream inconsistency. Less likely than projection/object handling, but still directly on the path of constructing the problematic predicate set.
